card.name: Present-perfect verbs after has/have
card.fires_on: The verb right after "has" or "have" (or sometimes "is"), such as been, occurred, resulted or received. It fires mostly in overdose, adverse-event and usage statements about a drug.

modes.label: Overdose reports
modes.description: "has/have occurred" or "resulted" in overdose or death statements.
modes.example: OVERDOSAGE Ceftazidime overdosage has<< occurred>> in patients with renal failure.

modes.label: Has been used/observed
modes.description: "has been" before used or observed in safety and experience statements.
modes.example: Terazosin has also<< been>> used in patients on a variety of con

modes.label: Non-drug general statements
modes.description: A linking verb in a general claim about a long-standing state of affairs.
modes.example: the Court has long held that affirmative action in higher education<< is>> uniquely privileged.

card.writes: It promotes words meaning originally, initially, formerly and at that time, and suppresses currently.
card.plain: It marks the verb after "has" or "have" when the text reports what has happened before, as in overdose or side-effect reports.
